Ensemble vote over detection series

Source: R/dfr_ensemble.R
ensemble_vote.Rd

Applies the voting of dfr_ensemble() to detection series computed beforehand, one column per detector (crisp ensemble with tolerance <= 1, fuzzy ensemble otherwise). This is how the paper combines its detectors.

Usage

ensemble_vote(
  detections,
  voting = c("majority", "efer", "threshold"),
  threshold = NULL,
  tolerance = 0,
  lookahead = TRUE
)

Arguments

detections

Logical (or 0/1) matrix or data frame, one row per time step and one column per detector.

voting

Voting rule: "majority" (default), "efer" or "threshold".

threshold

Vote needed by the "threshold" rule (lambda).

tolerance

Time tolerance k of the fuzzy scores; 0 (default) gives the crisp ensemble.

lookahead

With fuzzy scores, TRUE (default) uses detections on both sides of a time step, as in the paper. The vote of time t is then known only when t + k - 1 has arrived, so drifts are reported k - 1 observations after the time they refer to (obj$events holds those times). FALSE uses only the detections up to the current observation and reports at once.

Value

A logical vector with the ensemble drifts, with attribute vote (the vote of every time step, evaluated with the detections left after the earlier ensemble drifts).

Examples

detections <- matrix(FALSE, 100, 3)
detections[c(40, 43, 47), 1:3] <- diag(3) == 1
# No crisp majority: the detections are not simultaneous.
which(ensemble_vote(detections, "majority"))
#> integer(0)
# A fuzzy majority with a tolerance of 10 time steps.
which(ensemble_vote(detections, "majority", tolerance = 10))
#> [1] 39
